steps.what: Show the runbook steps already stored for this error id.
Provide technical guidance or support for development or troubleshooting of systems.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows runbook steps already stored for the error id. The systems engineer provides the technical guidance or the troubleshooting support. A step is not added when the id matches nothing. The runbook does not speak to the caller. An error with no stored step is answered by the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was a pasted runbook, including a step for a different error.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored steps for an error id can be shown. The guidance still comes from the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A caller whose error is not the one in the runbook still has to be heard.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer gives the guidance. The runbook is not the answer.
tasks.altitude: Guidance and troubleshooting stay with the engineer. The runbook only shows steps already stored for that error.

reach.task: Use guidance the engineer has given for this error.
reach.learn: A runbook step is not the guidance.

evidence.claim: Showing runbook steps for an error id is a lookup of text already stored. It does not provide the guidance.
An error id with no stored step does not get an invented answer. The engineer provides the support.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.

Fields: The error id and steps already stored for that id. Steps from a different error are not copied across. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the runbook in the document store before answering.
unknowns: Whether development questions and troubleshooting questions share one runbook.
research_questions: Who gives the guidance when the error belongs to another team's system?

already_counted.description: Providing the guidance and the troubleshooting support stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop runbook steps for errors on systems that have been retired.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still provides the technical guidance or the troubleshooting support. Only showing runbook steps already stored for that error id is removed. An error with no stored step saves none of the answer, and no step is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the request fields already captured for this information system.
Define and analyze objectives, scope, issues, and organizational impact.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} record shows request fields already captured. The systems engineer defines and analyzes the objectives, the scope, the issues, and the organisational impact of the information system. The request is not that analysis. A blank objective is not filled from a similar project.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives were copied from the last project because the request fields were a single sentence.
tasks.enabler_now: Captured request fields can be shown. Defining the objectives still takes the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: Impact on a team the request does not name has to be heard from that team.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer defines the objectives and the impact. The request fields are not the analysis.
tasks.altitude: Definition and analysis stay with the engineer. The captured request is only what was already written.

reach.task: Study an impact the engineer has defined.
reach.learn: A request field is not the objective.

evidence.claim: Showing captured request fields is a lookup. It does not define objectives or analyze impact.
A blank objective is not copied from another project. The engineer defines it.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.
Fields: The request id and fields already captured. Objectives are not invented to fill a blank. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the project request before the working session.
unknowns: Whether scope and organisational impact sit on the same request record.
research_questions: Who confirms impact when the affected team is outside this function?

already_counted.description: Defining and analyzing the objectives stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop request fields for projects that have been closed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still defines and analyzes objectives, scope, issues, and organisational impact. Only showing request fields already captured is removed. A blank objective saves nothing and is not copied from another project.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the operational standard already in force.
Establish functional or system standards and accept the text.
File the accepted functional or system standards.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the operational standard already in force. The systems engineer establishes the functional or system standard, including the quality requirements and the design constraints, and accepts the text. Only that version is filed. A constraint the current standard does not state is written by the engineer, not borrowed from another standard.
tasks.previous_blocker: A standard was republished with last year's constraints because nobody opened the current text.
tasks.enabler_now: The standard in force can be shown. Establishing the new text still takes the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A design constraint that operations and engineering disagree on is settled by the engineer, not by the old text.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer establishes the standard and accepts it. The current text is not the new one.
tasks.altitude: Establishing the standard stays with the engineer. Filing happens only after that text is accepted.

reach.task: Apply a standard the engineer has established and accepted.
reach.learn: The previous text is not the new standard.

evidence.claim: Showing the standard in force is a lookup. It does not establish the new standard.
The engineer writes and accepts the standard. Filing stores that version and does not publish a different one.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.

Fields: The standard id and the text already in force. A constraint is not copied from a different standard. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the current standard in the document store before editing.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the systems engineer.
unknowns: Whether quality requirements and design constraints live in one standard or several.
research_questions: Who else must accept a standard before it replaces the one in force?

already_counted.description: Establishing the standard and accepting the text stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Mark standards that this accepted text replaces.

approvals.approved_version: standard version and the standard id it replaces

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still establishes the functional or system standard and still accepts the text. Only showing the standard already in force, and filing the accepted version, is removed. A constraint the current text does not state is not borrowed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the constraints already recorded for this integration.
Develop the system or software architecture and accept it.
File the accepted architecture and the constraint ids.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows constraints already recorded for the integration. The systems engineer develops the system or software architecture, including a distributed design where that is what the constraints require, and accepts it. Only that version is filed. A constraint that is missing stops the file. The screen does not draw the architecture.
tasks.previous_blocker: An old diagram was reused, including a constraint this integration had dropped.
tasks.enabler_now: Recorded constraints can be shown. Developing the architecture still takes the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A distributed design that the constraints leave open is drawn by the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer develops the architecture and accepts it. The constraint list is not the drawing.
tasks.altitude: Architecture development stays with the engineer. Filing happens only after that version is accepted.

reach.task: Implement an architecture the engineer has developed and accepted.
reach.learn: A constraint list is not the architecture.

evidence.claim: Showing recorded constraints is a lookup. It does not develop the architecture.
The engineer develops and accepts the architecture. A generated diagram is not the accepted design.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.
Fields: The integration id and constraints already recorded. A missing constraint is not assumed away. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the constraint record before drawing.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the systems engineer.
unknowns: Whether system integration and distributed designs share one constraint record.
research_questions: Who accepts an architecture that crosses another team's system?

already_counted.description: Developing the architecture and accepting it stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop architectures whose constraints have been replaced.

approvals.approved_version: architecture version and the constraint ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still develops the system or software architecture and still accepts it. Only showing constraints already recorded, and filing the accepted version, is removed. A missing constraint saves nothing and is not assumed away.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The systems engineer still gives the guidance, still defines the objectives, and still writes the architecture. A stored runbook or a stored constraint can be opened. It does not answer the question or draw the architecture.
reach: Computer network support specialists take the call, and this job learns a runbook step is not the guidance.
Software developers implement an architecture, and this job learns the engineer still develops it.
skills_to_grow: Give guidance from what was asked, and do not invent a step the runbook does not have.
Define the objectives and the impact with the people who own the system.
Establish a standard, and file only the text just accepted.
role.ambitious_version: Guidance, objectives, standards, and architectures stay with the engineer. Stored runbooks and constraints only show what was already written.
